exercise1.prompt: How many of each, and the difference between size and count.

hiddenCases.name: it works on whichever column is named

exercise1.hint: value_counts on the column gives exactly this. to_dict() makes the keys and values plain, though the counts may need int() to shed their numpy type.

questions.prompt: How does value_counts order its result by default?
questions.explain: Frequency order, which is usually what you wanted to see. sort_index() gets you alphabetical when you need it.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between size and count on a group?
choices: size counts rows, count counts non-missing values
questions.explain: A group of three rows with one missing value has size 3 and count 2. Which is right depends on whether a gap is still a row to you.

questions.prompt: Why might a count come back as a numpy integer rather than a plain int?
choices: pandas stores columns as numpy types, so the values it hands back carry them
questions.explain: It behaves like an int almost everywhere, and it prints differently between library versions -- which is why the exercises here end in int().
